summary: This program builds a playlist of Song objects in an ArrayList, then sorts the same list three times — by title, by energy level from high to low, and by artist — printing the result after each sort.

lines.text: Comparator is the interface that describes how to compare two objects; the list's sort method needs one to know what order you want.

The variable's type is the List interface while the object is an ArrayList, which is the usual habit: you program against the general contract and keep the freedom to swap in another implementation later.
Each add appends one Song to the end of the list, so the starting order is simply the order the songs were added.
An enhanced for loop walks every element of the list in order, without you having to manage an index.

Comparator.comparing builds a comparator from a key: it calls getTitle on two songs and compares the resulting strings alphabetically. Note that sort rearranges the list itself rather than returning a new one.
forEach is the shorter alternative to a loop, and System.out::println is a method reference meaning "call println on each element."
comparingInt is the version for int keys; it avoids wrapping each number in an Integer object.
reversed flips the comparator's decision, turning low-to-high energy into high-to-low.
Sorting a third time discards the previous energy-level ordering, because each sort completely rearranges the one list.
